title: HVAC Service Call Estimate Worksheet
subtitle: Residential HVAC Service Call: prices observed scope, options, and exclusions.
description: HVAC Service Call Estimate Worksheet covers heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone. The home-service coordinator records Residential HVAC Service Call observed scope, costs, options, and terms. HVAC Service Call Estimate Worksheet keeps Residential HVAC Service Call exceptions visible until the home-service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use HVAC Service Call Estimate Worksheet at residence, equipment location, thermostat zone, and exterior unit area. Document heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone identity before Residential HVAC Service Call begins. Compare heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone findings with stated Residential HVAC Service Call criteria; route unresolved Residential HVAC Service Call issues to qualified HVAC technician. For HVAC Service Call Estimate Worksheet, confirm requirements for Residential HVAC Service Call. Ask qualified HVAC technician to review Residential HVAC Service Call conditions beyond the home-service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Property estimate review and customer identity
sections.guidance: Identify the customer, asset or property, estimator, and basis date before pricing the work.

blocks.label: Residential HVAC Service Call identity

fields.label: Equipment type, model, serial, and thermostat zone
Reported comfort issue, onset, prior service, and access condition

blocks.guidance: Use the Residential HVAC Service Call identifier printed on heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone or its linked source record.

sections.title: Pricing options and customer decision inputs
sections.guidance: Price the observable work and options. Keep concealed conditions and unconfirmed quantities out of fixed scope.

blocks.label: Residential HVAC Service Call scope observations
items: Thermostat call, displayed temperature, and mode response
Filter, airflow, register, and return condition
Indoor and outdoor unit visual condition
Condensate, drain, water, and icing observation
Electrical, fuel, venting, noise, and odor concern
Supply-return temperature or authorized performance result
blocks.guidance: Mark what was observed or supplied as estimate input; explain anything material that could not be inspected.

sections.title: Estimate exception and change conditions
sections.guidance: State what could change the price, timing, method, or scope before the customer or responsible party decides.

blocks.label: Do not proceed without control
blocks.guidance: Stop normal processing when a fuel, electrical, refrigerant, water, access, or safe-operation concern remains. Protect heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone; document the Residential HVAC Service Call notification and await qualified HVAC technician direction.

blocks.label: Conditions that may require a revised estimate or specialist review
items: Gas odor, combustion, damaged conductor, or water damage
System cannot be tested or restored safely
blocks.guidance: For Residential HVAC Service Call, identify affected heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone scope; ask home-service coordinator to document the Residential HVAC Service Call immediate control before continuing.

sections.title: Estimate decision and selected service scope
sections.guidance: Record the selected option and spending limit. Approval of an estimate authorizes only the stated scope and terms.

blocks.label: Estimate support retained
blocks.guidance: Attach or link proof for heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone; mark only Residential HVAC Service Call evidence present in that record.
